events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Central African Republic and CPJP over control of the government, starting 2009-11-26. This episode was active in 6 years (2009–2014), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2014-10-15.

events.title: Terrorist attack: 2009 Nevsky Express bombing
events.summary: The 2009 Nevsky Express bombing occurred on 27 November 2009 when a bomb exploded under a high speed train travelling between the Russian cities of Moscow and Saint Petersburg causing derailment near the town of Bologoye, Tver Oblast, on the Moscow–Saint Petersburg Railway. The derailment occurred at 21:34 local time.

events.title: Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 2009
events.summary: The 2009 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting was the 21st Meeting of the Heads of Government of the Commonwealth of Nations. It was held in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, between 27 and 29 November 2009, and was hosted by Prime Minister Patrick Manning.

events.title: 2009 New Democracy leadership election
events.summary: The 2009 New Democracy leadership election was held on 29 November 2009, following the official announcement of the resignation of Kostas Karamanlis, after more than 12 years as leader of New Democracy, the main centre-right political party and one of the two major parties in Greece.

events.title: 2009 Honduran general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Honduras on 29 November 2009, including presidential, parliamentary and local elections. Voters went to the polls to elect:A new President of Honduras to serve a four-year term starting on 27 January 2010. 128 members to serve a four-year term in the National Congress. Representatives in municipal (local) governments.

events.title: 2009 Swiss minaret referendum
events.summary: The federal popular initiative "against the construction of minarets" was a successful popular initiative in Switzerland to prevent the construction of minarets on mosques. In a November 2009 referendum, a constitutional amendment banning the construction of new minarets was approved by 57.5% of the participating voters.

events.title: 2009 Romanian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Romania in 2009. They were the sixth presidential elections held in post-1989 Romania. The first round took place on 22 November, with a run-off round between the top two candidates Traian Băsescu and Mircea Geoană on 6 December 2009.

events.title: Copenhagen climate summit
events.summary: The 2009 United Nations Climate Change Conference, commonly known as the Copenhagen Summit, was held at the Bella Center in Copenhagen, Denmark, between 7 and 18 December.

events.title: November–December 2009 Moldovan presidential election
events.summary: An indirect presidential election was held in Moldova on 10 November 2009 and 7 December 2009, following the parliamentary election held in July 2009.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Sweden.

events.title: 2009 Dominican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Dominica on 18 December 2009, to elect the 21 Representatives of the House of Assembly. The incumbent Dominica Labour Party increased its majority to 18 of 21 seats, winning a third term.

events.title: Sejdić and Finci v. Bosnia and Herzegovina
events.summary: Sejdić and Finci v. events.title: Terrorist attack: Northwest Airlines Flight 253
events.summary: The attempted bombing of Northwest Airlines Flight 253 occurred on December 25, 2009, aboard an Airbus A330 as it prepared to land at Detroit Metropolitan Airport following a transatlantic flight from Amsterdam.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Angola vs FLEC-FAC (Cabinda)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Angola and FLEC-FAC over control of Cabinda, starting 2009-12-31. This episode was active in 1 year (2009–2009), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2009-12-31.
